title: basic-auth issue detection invoke: UPDATE on the experiment is not enough, a body secret_id also needs USE on that gateway secret
answers: Why does issue detection return 403 for a secret I can see when I invoke it on my own experiment?
Which permission does the issues/invoke route check on the experiment and on the gateway secret it is given?
Where is the basic-auth gate for the issue-detection invoke route, and how does it treat an empty or unknown secret_id?
Can a user with only READ on a gateway secret run issue detection with it?
body:
Path: `POST /ajax-api/3.0/mlflow/issues/invoke` (issue detection, which runs a job in an experiment and can decrypt a gateway secret into the job environment) is gated in the basic-auth app by `mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:validate_can_invoke_issue_detection`, wired through the `(INVOKE_ISSUE_DETECTION, "POST")` entry of the before-request validator map. `genai/evaluate/invoke` and `scorer/invoke` are not affected.
Rule: The validator requires UPDATE on the body's `experiment_id` via `validate_can_update_experiment`, then, only when the body has a truthy `secret_id`, requires USE on that secret through `mlflow/server/auth/__init__.py:_get_gateway_secret_permission(secret_id).can_use`. The same helper backs `_get_permission_from_gateway_secret_id`, so workspace resolution and the default-permission floor match the gateway secret RPCs. An unknown secret id resolves to no grant and is denied, so the route does not reveal whether a secret exists.
Constraints: READ on the secret is not enough, and neither is ownership without a MANAGE/USE grant on the secret being checked by the route itself. An absent or empty `secret_id` passes the gate after the experiment check, because the handler (`_invoke_issue_detection_handler`) only fetches provider credentials when `secret_id` is truthy. Do not change the falsy guard to an `is None` check, because that would 403 requests the handler treats as having no secret. The validator reads the raw `secret_id` JSON key with `request.get_json(silent=True)`, not a proto parse, so any alias spelling of the field is not checked here. An endpoint_name passed to the same route is NOT checked against gateway-endpoint permissions; that is a known open gap.
Applies: Basic-auth authorization for issue-detection invoke requests, and any new invoke route that hands a gateway secret id to a job.
applies: Authorization for POST /ajax-api/3.0/mlflow/issues/invoke in the basic-auth app, including its optional secret_id and experiment_id body fields.
says: Running issue detection fails with access denied when selecting a credential with read access.
Users need permission to use the chosen gateway secret when launching issue detection.
Why is issue detection rejected when I can edit the experiment and view the secret?
Ensure starting an issue detection job validates permissions on both the experiment and secret.
search: In the basic-auth app, POST /ajax-api/3.0/mlflow/issues/invoke (INVOKE_ISSUE_DETECTION) uses validate_can_invoke_issue_detection to require UPDATE on experiment_id and, when secret_id is truthy, USE on that secret via _get_gateway_secret_permission(secret_id).can_use. READ permission or secret ownership without a USE grant is insufficient, and an unknown secret ID is denied without revealing whether the secret exists. An absent or empty secret_id passes after experiment validation because _invoke_issue_detection_handler only fetches credentials when secret_id is truthy. The route reads raw secret_id JSON rather than protobuf, does not check endpoint_name against endpoint permissions, and does not affect genai/evaluate/invoke or scorer/invoke.
